source.title: Friend or Foe: How LLMs’ Safety Mind Gets Fooled by Intent Shift Attack
source.authors: Peng Ding; Jun Kuang; Wen-Show Sun; Zong-Yu Wang; Xue-Zhi Cao; Xun-Liang Cai; Jia-Jun Chen; Shujian Huang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign-data fine-tuning raises harmful compliance, using ISA-reformulated benign data rather than the original study’s fine-tuning recipe.
record.gate_note: The study tests benign fine-tuning on two models and reports harmful-completion rates. Its ISA attacks and intent-classification results concern intent-shift attacks, not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or response-position KL; they do not test those mechanisms or the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: Section 4.3 fine-tunes Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 500 benign Q&A pairs rewritten with ISA templates. It reports harmful-completion rates (GPT-ASR) before and after, which bears on V2 with a different benign-data recipe than the original. The ISA attack results in Table 2 are prompt-rephrasing jailbreaks, not prefills, suffixes or decoding changes, so they do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that intent-shifting rephrasings bypass safety because models misread intent as benign knowledge-seeking. Benign ISA-styled fine-tuning pushes ASR to near 100%. Existing defenses are inconsistent, and stronger defenses raise over-refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 500 benign daily-request samples rewritten with ISA templates and fine-tunes with LoRA; it does not reproduce the original harmful-example fine-tuning procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by ISA shift type, benchmark, and model (Table 2).

fits_no_version.finding: Minimal intent-shifting rephrasings (person, tense, voice, mood, question) raise GPT-ASR from 0–4% to roughly 22–86% across five models, including Claude-4-Sonnet and GPT-4.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety refusal is keyed to surface intent cues in the prompt, so linguistic rephrasing without added context bypasses it.

fits_no_version.finding: In Table 3, models classify 94–99% of ISA prompts as general knowledge inquiries, versus about 99–100% correctly labelled harmful for the original prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success under intent shift tracks misclassified user intent.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The benign fine-tuning comparison covers two models and 50 transformed test prompts; uncertainty estimates are not reported. Fine-tuning uses ISA-reformulated data, so it does not establish the effect of ordinary benign instruction data alone.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported Table 2 ISA attack-rate results were omitted; the 50 entries are recorded as findings on intent-shift attacks, not as tests of the specified mechanisms in V4.

untested.parts: Ordinary benign data without ISA phrasing; harmful compliance on plain, untransformed harmful prompts after fine-tuning; other models, data sizes and hyperparameters (only lr 1e-3, 10 epochs, LoRA r=8); capability after fine-tuning.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial-suffix or decoding attacks on the target models; GCG appears only as a baseline in Table 7.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
The FT defense trains intent analysis, not safety spread beyond the first tokens; not tested.

missing.what: Vanilla (untransformed) GPT-ASR on the fine-tuning test set: Qwen 2%, Llama 0%. Post-fine-tuning ASR on untransformed prompts is not reported.
Intention-classification results; defense results (Tables 5–6), including XSTest over-refusal rising from 4% to 25% under the FT defense.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. V2 evidence comes from a single setting: two small models, n=50, one hyperparameter set (lr 1e-3, 10 epochs), GPT-4o judge, no variance. The benign data shares the attack's surface form, so it tests 'carefully chosen' benign data, not ordinary data. Rows R1–R50 correctly carry no version link.

versions.untested_parts: Tests 500 benign samples rewritten with ISA templates on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; does not test ordinary benign data without ISA reformulation or other models and data sizes.
Tests intent-shift attacks, not prefilling a compliant opening, suffix attacks, or decoding changes.
No localization of safety to weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Does not test training to spread safety across response tokens or whether such training holds up.

relationships.condition: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, LoRA fine-tuned on 500 benign ISA-templated samples, evaluated on 50 ISA-transformed harmful prompts
relationships.reason: GPT-ASR rose from 56% to 100% (Qwen) and from 48% to 96% (Llama) after benign-only fine-tuning (R51, R52).
relationships.display_finding: GPT-judged ASR rose from 56% to 100% for Qwen and from 48% to 96% for Llama.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, LoRA fine-tuned on 500 benign ISA-templated samples, evaluated on 50 ISA-transformed harmful prompts
source_check.reason: R51 and R52 correctly report GPT-ASR rising from 56% to 100% and from 48% to 96%, respectively, after benign-only fine-tuning.

relationships.condition: Benign data deliberately matched to the attack's phrasing templates
relationships.reason: The rise is shown only on prompts phrased like the training data (R51, R52). Whether generic benign data or plain harmful prompts show the effect is not measured.
relationships.display_finding: Compliance rose on prompts phrased like the training data; the study did not measure generic benign data or plain harmful prompts.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Benign data deliberately matched to the attack's phrasing templates
source_check.reason: R51 and R52 support V2 in the tested setting. Generic benign training and post-fine-tuning evaluation on plain harmful prompts are untested; no comparison establishes dependence on template matching. Untested conditions do not justify limits_scope.
